from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of 'Perspective'", [
            "A basis is just a set of coordinate axes.",
            "Vectors exist independently of our chosen basis.",
            "Coordinates depend entirely on that chosen basis."
        ])

        # Animation Setup
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_color": WHITE, "stroke_opacity": 0.5})
        vec_i = Vector(RIGHT, color="#FF4500")
        vec_j = Vector(UP, color="#FF4500")
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(grid.c2p(1, 1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(grid, "A4", "D6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(grid))
        self.play(grid.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(vec_i, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(vec_j, "B5")
        self.play(Create(vec_i), Create(vec_j))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        # Perspective shift effect using rotation and color
        self.play(grid.animate.set_color("#00CED1").rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT),
                  vec_i.animate.set_color("#ADFF2F").rotate(PI/6),
                  vec_j.animate.set_color("#ADFF2F").rotate(PI/6))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Basis Transformation", [
            "We compare a standard basis with a custom one.",
            "Grid lines warp to represent the new basis.",
            "Space is unchanged, only our ruler changes."
        ])

        # Animation Setup
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        i_hat = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        j_hat = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        basis_group = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat)
        
        v1 = np.array([1.5, 0.5, 0])
        v2 = np.array([-0.5, 1.2, 0])
        
        v1_arrow = Arrow(ORIGIN, v1, color="#1E90FF", buff=0)
        v2_arrow = Arrow(ORIGIN, v2, color="#1E90FF", buff=0)
        new_basis_group = VGroup(v1_arrow, v2_arrow)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.add(plane)
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))
        # Warp logic (simulated by transforming plane)
        new_plane = plane.copy().apply_matrix([[1.5, -0.5], [0.5, 1.2]])
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(plane, new_plane), 
                  ReplacementTransform(basis_group, new_basis_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Highlight space property
        self.play(Indicate(new_plane))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Change-of-Basis Matrix", [
            "The transition matrix maps between different bases.",
            "Construct columns from new basis vectors.",
            "It acts as a translator for coordinates."
        ])
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        # Matrix P definition
        matrix_tex = MathTex(
            "P = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\\\ 1 & 1 \\end{pmatrix}"
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_tex, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix_tex))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # Highlight columns
        # Column 1
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_tex[0][4:8], color="#FF6347")
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_tex[0][8:12], color="#9370DB")
        
        self.play(Create(col1_rect), Create(col2_rect))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        # Matrix multiplication action
        eq_tex = MathTex("P \\vec{x}_C = \\vec{x}_B")
        self.place_at_grid(eq_tex, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_tex))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Formula and Application", [
            "Coordinates relate via [v]_B = P[v]_C.", 
            "Inverse matrices reverse the coordinate conversion.", 
            "This powers systems like self-driving car navigation."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"[v]_B = P [v]_C", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        inv_formula = MathTex(r"[v]_C = P^{-1} [v]_B", font_size=40, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(inv_formula, "C2")
        self.play(Write(inv_formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF8C00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        gps_label = Text("Navigation System", font_size=24, color="#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(gps_label, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(gps_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective' (Prerequisite Review)
sections.content: Recall that a basis is a set of 'coordinate axes' (basis vectors). Explain that a vector exists independently, but its coordinates depend on the chosen basis. Use a visual of a point in 2D space described by (x, y) relative to standard grid lines.
sections.example: Imagine a robot looking at a fruit bowl. If the robot moves, its 'forward' and 'right' axes shift. The fruit's location remains the same, but the coordinate numbers change.

sections.title: Visualizing the Basis Transformation
sections.content: Introduce two bases: Basis B (standard, e.g., i, j) and Basis C (custom, e.g., v1, v2). Use an animation where the grid lines warp from square (standard) to slanted/stretched (new basis). Emphasize that the space hasn't changed, only the ruler we use to measure it.
sections.example: Representing a vector v=[3, 2] in the standard grid, then overlaying a new red grid (Basis C) to see how those same coordinates translate into new numbers [a, b].

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the Transition Matrix (P). Explain that P maps coordinates from Basis C to Basis B. Show the matrix construction: columns are the coordinates of the new basis vectors expressed in the old basis.
sections.example: If Basis C is defined by vectors v1=[1, 1] and v2=[-1, 1], the matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] acts as a 'translator' for any coordinate pair.

sections.title: The Formula and Application
sections.content: Present the core equation: [v]_B = P[v]_C. Explain that to go the other way, we need the inverse matrix (P^-1). Connect this to real-world navigation systems.
sections.example: A GPS satellite uses a global basis, but a self-driving car uses its own local 'body-centric' basis. The car uses a change-of-basis matrix to convert global coordinates into its own local 'drive-straight-ahead' instructions.
